walls.note: Brussels second wall (1356-83), the 'pentagon', with seven main gates and the Oeverpoort of 1561 at the Willebroek canal basin. Ring through the gate positions taken from OSM (gate squares and the surviving Hallepoort) along today's inner ring, which follows the wall line; checked against the Ferraris map (1777), where the main rampart lies within about 50 m of this line. The outer bastions and Fort Monterey (1672-75) are later and not included.

landmarks.y1650: Gothic town hall (1401-55) on the Grote Markt; its 96 m tower by Jan van Ruysbroeck carries the gilded Saint Michael slaying the dragon (1455). The Grote Markt's guild houses of 1650 were destroyed in the French bombardment of 1695.
landmarks.special: Saint Michael and the dragon; main bell tower

landmarks.y1650: Ducal bread hall, rebuilt 1504-36 (Keldermans); the present building is a reconstruction of 1873-95 on the same plot.
Collegiate church of Saints Michael and Gudula (Gothic, towers finished 1485); a cathedral only since 1962.
Palace of the dukes of Brabant on the Coudenberg, court of the governor Leopold Wilhelm in 1650; burnt in 1731 (site under today's Koningsplein).
Romanesque-Gothic church of the Marollen; Pieter Bruegel the Elder is buried here (1569).
Late-Gothic church of the crossbowmen's guild on the Zavel.
Great beguinage in the north-west of the town; its present baroque church dates from 1657-76, so in 1650 the older church stood.
Bronze fountain figure by Jérôme Duquesnoy the Elder, 1619.
Gate of the second wall (1381), used as a prison; the only surviving gate.
Tower of the first wall (13th c.).
